claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang@stage-0: db/seed.sql l.24-35 (12 orders), l.51-59 (8 payments, one per order at most), l.16-22 (5 customers)

claims.text: At stage-0, customer 1 (Trần Minh Anh) has three payments, of 2150000, 890000 and 1730000 đồng, on orders 1, 2 and 10.

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, count, sum, avg, min and max are aggregate functions: they compute one result from many input rows.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §9.21 Aggregate Functions, table 9.60

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, count(*) counts input rows, while count(expression) counts the rows where the expression is not NULL.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §9.21 Aggregate Functions, table 9.60 (count(*) vs count(expression))

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, coalesce returns the first of its arguments that is not NULL.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §9.18.2 COALESCE

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17 a query is processed FROM and its joins, then WHERE, then GROUP BY, then the aggregates, then HAVING, then ORDER BY; that is the order the result is defined by, not the plan the server uses.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §7.1-§7.5 Queries (Table Expressions, WHERE, GROUP BY and HAVING, Select Lists, Sorting Rows)

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, WHERE is applied before grouping and may not contain an aggregate function; such a query is rejected with an error.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §2.7 Aggregate Functions and §7.2.2 The WHERE Clause

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, GROUP BY collects the rows that share values in the grouped columns and the result holds one row per group; each aggregate is computed over the rows of its own group.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §7.2.3 The GROUP BY and HAVING Clauses

claims.text: With GROUP BY present, PostgreSQL 17 rejects a select-list reference to an ungrouped column outside an aggregate, except when the column is functionally dependent on the grouped columns — notably when a table's primary key is grouped.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §7.2.3 (functional dependency on a primary key) and SELECT reference page, GROUP BY clause

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, HAVING is applied after grouping and after the aggregates are computed, and it removes whole groups; its condition may use aggregates and, outside an aggregate, may reference only grouped columns, as the select list must.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §7.2.3 The GROUP BY and HAVING Clauses

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, sum over a group in which every input value is NULL, or over no rows at all, returns NULL rather than zero.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §9.21 Aggregate Functions (aggregates ignore NULL inputs; sum returns null when there are no non-null inputs)

claims.text: The second query of the file returns 2 rows at stage-0: Trần Minh Anh 4770000 and Lê Quốc Dũng 2140000; his total in the first query is 3150000, the difference being his cod payment of 1010000 on order 5.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang@stage-0: db/queries/revenue-by-customer.sql l.16-24 against db/seed.sql l.51-59 (payments 1, 2, 7 are card for customer 1; payment 5 card, payment 4 cod for customer 3)

claims.text: Customers 2 and 4 have no payment with method 'card' at stage-0 — customer 2's two payments are 'bank_transfer' and 'cod', and customer 4's only payment is the 'bank_transfer' on order 8 — so WHERE removes all their rows and they form no group in the second query.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang@stage-0: db/seed.sql l.51-59 (payments 3 bank_transfer and 8 cod belong to customer 2; payment 6 bank_transfer to customer 4)

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, ORDER BY and GROUP BY may name an output column, while HAVING's condition is documented as referencing grouping columns and aggregates over input columns, as WHERE does.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs SELECT reference page: GROUP BY clause, HAVING clause, ORDER BY clause

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, moving the condition p.method = 'card' into HAVING while grouping only by c.full_name is rejected, because method is then neither grouped nor inside an aggregate.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §7.2.3 The GROUP BY and HAVING Clauses (HAVING may reference only grouped columns and aggregates)

claims.text: Adding o.status to the select list of the first query, without adding it to GROUP BY or wrapping it in an aggregate, is rejected by PostgreSQL 17: o.status is neither grouped nor inside an aggregate, and the grouped columns are customers' primary key, not orders'.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §7.2.3 (a grouped table's ungrouped columns cannot be referenced outside an aggregate) and SELECT reference page, GROUP BY clause

claims.text: psql is PostgreSQL's terminal client and prints the row count under each result; scripts/sql/run-query.sh <name> runs db/queries/<name>.sql against the lab database with psql.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang@stage-0: scripts/sql/run-query.sh l.7-11; PostgreSQL 17 psql reference, \pset footer (the "(n rows)" count in the default aligned format)

claims.text: Raising the threshold on line 23 of the query file from 2000000 to 3000000 leaves one row in the second result, Trần Minh Anh at 4770000, and changes nothing in the first result.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang@stage-0: db/queries/revenue-by-customer.sql l.23; card totals 4770000 and 2140000 from db/seed.sql l.51-59

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, WHERE keeps only the rows whose condition is true, and a comparison such as p.method = 'card' is not true of a row whose p.method is NULL, so WHERE drops that row.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs §7.2.2 The WHERE Clause (rows for which the condition is true are kept) and §9.2 Comparison Functions and Operators (a comparison with NULL yields null)
